hints: Focus on what actually remains at equilibrium, not what you started with, and remember the mole ratio links them together.
Since 0.100 mol of $\text{SO}_3$ has formed, work out how much $\text{SO}_2$ and $\text{O}_2$ must have reacted to make it.
Put the equilibrium concentrations into the $K_c$ expression with the correct powers, then check the units cancel to guide you to the right value.
walkthrough:
**Find the equilibrium moles using the mole ratio**

Think of it like a recipe. Making 2 moles of product uses up 2 moles of $\text{SO}_2$ and 1 mole of $\text{O}_2$.

$$2\text{SO}_2 + \text{O}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2\text{SO}_3$$

**Subtract reacted, keep remaining**

To make 0.100 mol of $\text{SO}_3$, you must use 0.100 mol of $\text{SO}_2$ and half as much $\text{O}_2$, which is 0.050 mol.

$$n(\text{SO}_2)_{eq} = 0.200 - 0.100 = 0.100 \text{ mol}$$
$$n(\text{O}_2)_{eq} = 0.200 - 0.050 = 0.150 \text{ mol}$$
$$n(\text{SO}_3)_{eq} = 0.100 \text{ mol}$$

**Convert to concentrations**

Volume is $1.00 \text{ dm}^3$, so concentration in $\text{mol dm}^{-3}$ is numerically the same as moles. That keeps the maths friendly.

$$[\text{SO}_2] = 0.100 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}, [\text{O}_2] = 0.150 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}, [\text{SO}_3] = 0.100 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$$

**Apply the $K_c$ expression and units**

Products go on top, reactants below, each raised to its balancing number.

$$K_c = \frac{[\text{SO}_3]^2}{[\text{SO}_2]^2[\text{O}_2]} = \frac{(0.100)^2}{(0.100)^2(0.150)} = \frac{1}{0.150} = 6.67$$
Units: $\frac{(\text{mol dm}^{-3})^2}{(\text{mol dm}^{-3})^2(\text{mol dm}^{-3})} = \text{mol}^{-1} \text{dm}^3$.

options.A: This is the reciprocal of the correct $K_c$, about 0.150. It comes from flipping the expression upside down to $\frac{[\text{SO}_2]^2[\text{O}_2]}{[\text{SO}_3]^2}$. Remember products always go on top for $K_c$.
options.B: This combines two errors: using starting concentrations instead of equilibrium concentrations, and then inverting the expression. Starting amounts do not represent equilibrium position.
options.C: This uses the correct $K_c$ expression but the initial concentrations of $\text{SO}_2$ (0.200) and $\text{O}_2$ (0.200). You must first subtract what reacted to find the true equilibrium values of 0.100 and 0.150.
options.D: Correct. With equilibrium concentrations 0.100, 0.150 and 0.100 $\text{mol dm}^{-3}$, $K_c = (0.100)^2 / [(0.100)^2(0.150)] = 6.67 \text{ mol}^{-1} \text{dm}^3$.
